(a) SCHEDULER FIRING ARCHITECTURE: no docs/migration/decisions/*.md record settles what fires a deferred timer (Oban vs a supervised per-timer process vs a polling GenServer); mix.exs has neither Oban nor Quantum. The first batch cited this as its reason for deferring scheduler. It is now MUCH more tractable than 'wide open', and the draft must say so: R-Co's SCH-02 (docs/requirements.yaml, RELEASED) specifies the mechanism concretely -- a background poller at a configurable interval (default 5s, env-var configurable), selecting status=PENDING AND fire_at <= NOW(), firing each due timer in a SINGLE transaction that marks it FIRED and appends the instance event, and in clustered deployments taking a PostgreSQL ADVISORY LOCK on the timer id before processing (skip if unavailable, released at commit). Edge cases are specified too (DB unavailable -> rollback, stays PENDING, retried next poll; a timer due between polls fires next poll, max latency = interval + jitter). SCH-06 adds jitter, SCH-05 requires overdue timers carry fired_late:true with scheduled-vs-actual timestamps and that NONE is skipped or double-fired. THE CANONICALISER QUESTION ORCH FLAGGED, answered with evidence rather than preference: REQ-202 must NOT extend lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_digest.ex. So REQ-202 builds a separate module and requires BOTH moduledocs to cross-reference each other saying why two canonicalisers exist deliberately -- two by accident is the failure mode, two by a recorded decision is correct. issues.detail: SCH-02's literal text mandates a per-timer PostgreSQL advisory lock, but R-Co REMOVED that mechanism. src/design/scheduler-concurrency-epic3.md's ISS-301 section deletes the pg_try_advisory_xact_lock block (scheduler.zig L207-242) as redundant against FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, on four stated grounds. Only a SESSION-level lock (fixed constant 5863412975429063421) guarding the ISS-302 startup sweep survives. ORCH's brief assumed the advisory lock was the shipped mechanism; it is not. REQ-185 carries the correction so a port does not reintroduce deleted code.

R-Co's src/expr is NOT a CEL implementation. EXP-102's cutover went FROM vendor/cel TO src/expr, retiring CEL. Its real surface (ast.zig L12-60 and L83-150, lexer.zig L17-32) is: arithmetic + - * / % and unary negation, the 6 comparison operators (non-chainable), and/or/not as word keywords, int/float/string/bool/null literals, dotted variable paths, and exactly 11 whitelisted builtins (length, lower, upper, trim, contains, startsWith, endsWith, coalesce, now, date_add, date_diff). It has no 'in', no ternary, no list/map literals, no indexing, and none of the CEL macros, type-conversion functions or collection functions. ORCH's brief framed those as the genuine gap versus R-Co; they are CEL vocabulary neither system implements. expr.ex's @unsupported_call_markers therefore stays correct as-is, and REQ-197/198 are scoped to what R-Co actually has.

The brief asked whether any of these six subsystems has an already-committed SPA consumer. THREE do. web/src/api/services.ts defines ServiceRecord plus all five routes and is consumed by pages/admin/services/ServicesPage.tsx. web/src/api/metrics.ts defines parsePrometheusText and calls client.getText('/metrics'), consumed by pages/admin/MetricsPage.tsx. web/src/api/audit.ts declares RawAuditEntry with before_state/after_state, consumed by pages/admin/AuditLogPage.tsx. The metrics one is decisive on one of REQ-078's three recorded divergences: the SPA already parses Prometheus TEXT at an unversioned /metrics, not JSON at /api/v1/metrics. Cited as the binding contract in REQ-191/192, REQ-194 and REQ-196 respectively, the same way REQ-181/182 did.

Three R-Co secrets defects verified directly and explicitly scoped against in REQ-189/190 rather than inherited: (a) the master key is a hardcoded 64-zero hex literal at four call sites (api/routes/webhooks.zig:375, webhook/dispatcher.zig:537, webhook/subscription_store.zig:224, effects/worker.zig:42) and a grep for MASTER_KEY or WRAPPING_KEY across R-Co's whole src/ returns ZERO matches, so the env wiring EXP-501 describes was never built; (b) rows are written with wrapped_key_algorithm 'aes_kw_256' while crypto.zig's own comment states it performs a second AES-GCM pass instead, so the stored metadata is false; (c) the unpinned lookup takes the newest row rather than the newest ACTIVE version, so disabling the newest version breaks resolution instead of falling back.

REQ-191 proposes service_catalog as a GLOBAL table, departing from decision 0003 Decision B's general per-tenant-schema rule. The R-Co-grounded reason is structural, not incidental: a scope='global' entry is by definition referenceable by every tenant, and service_id is globally unique across tenants, so neither property is expressible in a per-tenant copy. The requirement states the reason and requires REVIEWER sign-off rather than diverging quietly. REQ-189 likewise requires an explicit placement decision for the secrets table, which R-Co also makes global. Both flagged per CLAUDE.md's do-not-silently-re-decide rule.
